patterns: Age‑specific direct address that tells viewers what to stop or start doing, often paired with a strong emoji
Bold promise of a single, counter‑intuitive lesson framed as a “why/what” question
Use of a short, punchy hook (≤6 words) that hints at a payoff and triggers curiosity
Fast‑paced opening that cites a vivid quote or stark fact within the first 3 seconds
Emotional blend of practicality and spiritual/faith reassurance that resonates with older audiences
title_formulas: After ___, You Must ___ – ___ Tips in ___ Seconds
opening_3s: Show a striking line from a classic text while a bold on‑screen graphic flashes “STOP DOING THIS!”
Cut to a close‑up of a ticking clock and say “You’ve only got ___ seconds to change ___ forever.”
Begin with a quick personal anecdote: “At ___ years old I learned this one truth…”
comment_themes: Viewers love age‑related validation and practical wisdom they can apply now
Requests for more specific book titles or deeper philosophical context
Appreciation for spiritual/faith references that reinforce the lesson
Calls for clearer thumbnails and on‑screen text so the key message sticks
avoid: Generic, vague titles without a numeric or age hook
Videos longer than 60 seconds without a clear, fast‑moving structure
Overusing jargon or obscure references that alienate casual viewers
try_next: Launch a "Decade‑by‑Decade Stoic Hacks" series, each 30‑second clip targeting a specific age range
Combine split‑screen of original public‑domain text with modern animation, ending with a one‑sentence actionable tip
Add a pinned comment summarizing the lesson and prompting viewers to share their own experience in the comments
